issues.title: Correct the scaffold brief's frontend tree before scaffolding from it
issues.scope: SCAFFOLD_BRIEF.md lists four page files and says to use create-next-app defaults while also forbidding anything extra. Those two instructions conflict, and the tree omits app/layout.tsx, which the App Router requires. Fix the brief before anyone builds from it, rather than discovering the contradiction mid-scaffold.
acceptance: Verify against a real create-next-app run what the App Router actually requires and what the default output contains; paste the file list
The tree is corrected to include every required file, at minimum a root layout, and the PR states what was missing
The contradiction between create-next-app defaults and nothing extra is resolved with explicit wording about which generated files are kept
The brief states that the frontend gate FR-24 blocks route content but not the scaffold itself, since the scaffold is structure rather than UI

issues.title: Scaffold the Next.js application
issues.scope: Create the app skeleton with the four routes as placeholders only. FR-24 blocks real UI until E13-12 closes, so these routes carry a heading and nothing else.
acceptance: TypeScript, app router, strict mode enabled
Each route renders a heading and a one-line comment naming the issue that will implement it; no layout work, no wallet code, no API calls
`npm install`, `npm run dev`, `npm run build` and typecheck all succeed; paste the output for each
The tree matches the corrected brief exactly; list any difference and justify it
`git status` confirms nothing outside lumens-vault/frontend/ changed
nonGoals: No real UI. No styling decisions. No wallet integration.

issues.title: Add frontend configuration and fail-fast validation
issues.scope: The frontend needs the backend URL, the contract id, the network passphrase and an RPC URL. A missing contract id that silently defaults produces an app that looks like it works and shows nothing, which is worse than a startup failure.
acceptance: All settings come from environment variables; nothing is hardcoded, including the contract id
Validation runs at startup and fails visibly with a message naming the missing variable rather than rendering a broken page
Only values safe for the browser are exposed to the client bundle; state which are public and why each is safe
.env.example lists every variable with a comment and no real values
The contract id matches the one in docs/deployments.md; a mismatch between frontend and backend must be detectable, so both are displayed somewhere in the UI
nonGoals: No secrets in the frontend at all.

issues.title: Build the typed API client
issues.scope: One place that talks to the backend, with types matching docs/api.md. Amounts arrive as strings and must stay strings or bigint through the client — a single implicit conversion to a JavaScript number silently corrupts large balances.
acceptance: Types mirror the documented API responses exactly
Amount fields are typed as string or bigint, never number, and a test asserts a large amount survives a round trip unchanged
Network failures and non-2xx responses produce typed errors distinguishing backend-unreachable from backend-returned-an-error, since the UI treats them differently
A 429 is surfaced distinctly so the UI can back off rather than retry immediately
No component calls fetch directly; all traffic goes through this client
nonGoals: No data-fetching library choice imposed here.

issues.title: Detect Freighter and handle it being absent
issues.scope: Freighter is a browser extension and most first-time visitors will not have it. Detection must handle the extension injecting asynchronously, which is a common source of false negatives on first paint.
acceptance: Detects whether Freighter is installed without throwing when it is not
Handles the extension becoming available after initial page load rather than deciding once and caching a false negative
The not-installed state renders the design from E13-08, including where to get it
Server-side rendering does not break — the check must not run during SSR, and the PR states how that is ensured
Tests cover present, absent, and late-injection

issues.title: Implement wallet connection and disconnection
issues.scope: Connect, expose the public key, and disconnect. User rejection is a normal outcome and must not surface as an error state.
acceptance: Connecting requests access and stores the returned public key
User rejection returns the app to the disconnected state quietly, with no error banner
Disconnect clears all wallet state and any cached user data, so the next user does not see the previous one's vaults
Connection state survives a page refresh if the wallet is still authorised, and the mechanism is stated
Tests cover success, rejection, and the extension erroring

issues.title: Detect and handle network mismatch
issues.scope: A wallet on mainnet against a testnet contract shows an empty, apparently-working app. Worse, a user could sign a transaction intended for a different network. This check must be prominent and blocking.
acceptance: The wallet's network is read and compared against configuration on connection and whenever it changes
A mismatch blocks all transaction actions and displays which network is required, per the E13-08 design
It must never present as an empty portfolio; a test asserts the mismatch state takes precedence over rendering empty data
Network switching in the wallet is detected without requiring a page reload
Tests cover match, mismatch, and a switch while connected

issues.title: Implement transaction signing and submission
issues.scope: Build, simulate, sign and submit contract invocations, then wait for confirmation. This is shared by deposit and withdraw, so it lives here rather than being written twice.
acceptance: Transactions are simulated before signing so a failure that is going to happen is caught before the user is asked to approve
A simulation failure maps the contract error code to a readable message using the error list in docs/contract-interface.md
The correct network passphrase is used; a test asserts it comes from configuration rather than a default

Submission polls for confirmation with a timeout, and a timeout is reported as unknown rather than failed — the transaction may still land, and telling a user it failed when it succeeded is the worst outcome
User rejection at the signing step is handled quietly
Tests cover simulation failure, rejection, success, and confirmation timeout

issues.title: Map contract error codes to user-facing messages
issues.scope: The contract returns numeric error codes. Showing a user Error 5 is useless; showing them that their lock has not expired is actionable. The mapping must be kept in step with the contract's enum.
acceptance: Every error variant in docs/contract-interface.md has a message that says what happened and what the user can do
An unrecognised code degrades to a generic message including the raw code, rather than showing nothing
A test asserts the mapping covers every documented variant, so a contract adding an error without a message fails
Messages avoid blame and jargon — TimelockNotExpired becomes a statement about the unlock date, not an error name
A comment records that error codes must never be renumbered once deployed, and that this mapping is why

issues.title: Build the shared amount and decimals utilities
issues.scope: Amounts are i128 strings scaled by per-asset decimals. Every display and every input conversion goes through here, because doing it ad hoc in components is how precision bugs get everywhere.
acceptance: Formatting takes a raw string amount and the asset's decimals and returns a display string; it never accepts or produces a JavaScript number
Parsing user input returns a raw string amount, rejecting more decimal places than the asset supports rather than truncating silently
Decimals are always passed in, never assumed — a test covers assets with seven and six decimals producing different output for the same raw value
Values beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER format correctly; this test is the reason the module exists
Rounding behaviour for display is stated and never rounds up, so a displayed balance is never more than the real one

issues.title: Build the ledger-to-time utilities
issues.scope: The contract works in ledger sequence numbers; users think in dates. The conversion assumes five seconds per ledger, which is an average rather than a guarantee, and the resulting imprecision must be honest rather than hidden.
acceptance: Converts a ledger difference to a human duration and an unlock ledger to an approximate date
The five-seconds-per-ledger assumption is stated in one place and used everywhere
Output is presented as approximate; a test asserts the formatting conveys that rather than implying a precise timestamp
Durations under one ledger, and past unlock ledgers, both render sensibly rather than as negative time
A comment notes that ledger close times vary, so a countdown will drift and must not be presented as exact

issues.title: Implement the app shell and navigation
issues.scope: The layout every route sits inside: navigation, wallet status, and the global banners for paused contract and stale backend.
acceptance: Navigation covers all four routes with the active one indicated
Wallet connection state and the connected address are always visible
A global banner shows when the contract is paused, since it affects every action
A global banner shows when the backend is significantly behind or unreachable, so no page silently shows stale data
The network in use is displayed, so a testnet deployment is never mistaken for mainnet
Keyboard navigation works through the whole shell, per E13-10

issues.title: Implement shared loading and error components
issues.scope: Every view loads and every view can fail. Building these once keeps behaviour consistent and stops each page inventing its own spinner and error text.
acceptance: Loading, error and empty components match the E13-09 specification
The error component distinguishes backend-unreachable from a real error and offers a retry where retrying could help
An error boundary prevents one failing section from blanking the whole page
Components are accessible: loading state is announced to assistive technology, errors are associated with what failed
No component shows a raw exception message to the user

issues.title: Verify the frontend foundation end to end
issues.scope: Checkpoint before feature work: the app runs, connects a real wallet, reads from a real backend, and handles the failure paths that will otherwise be discovered one at a time during E15.
acceptance: A real Freighter wallet connects against the deployed testnet contract; state the browser and extension version
Wrong-network detection is verified by actually switching the wallet to mainnet and confirming the app blocks and explains
The app runs with the backend stopped and shows the unreachable state rather than crashing
`npm run build` produces a production build with zero TypeScript errors
The README covers setup, configuration and the wallet requirement, with every command actually run
nonGoals: No feature pages; those are E15.
